Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.server

Class Protection

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.server.Protection
public final class Protection extends Object
Server-authoritative protection consults for the mod's packet-driven player gestures. The mod's custom packets take the place of the vanilla interactions the client suppresses, so these re-run the checks a vanilla interaction would have triggered: world border, spawn protection, and the right-click interaction event that claim and logging mods hook.

Growth and removal driven by automation, and the vanilla mechanics behind them, live in the loader-neutral WorldEdits instead; this class is only the player-packet-facing half, which stays Forge-specific because it fires PlayerInteractEvent.RightClickBlock.

The vanilla click a gesture displaces

A gesture reaches the server twice. The client sends the mod's own packet from inside its RightClickBlock handler, and then the vanilla ServerboundUseItemOnPacket for the same click follows. Both are enqueued onto the server task queue in arrival order, so the mod's packet is handled first, in the same tick. Everything below rests on that:
  • A gesture that claims a click must mark RightClickBlockSuppressor for the position it claimed, so the vanilla click that follows cannot also act there. The mark lives one tick, matching the lifetime of the displaced click.
  • The mark vetoes RightClickBlock at that position, and the consults here fire that same event. A consult run after the mark would therefore refuse itself, so the mark is always placed last.
The claim methods below exist to make that ordering structural: they run every consult and only then mark. No caller places a mark of its own.

  • Method Details

    • claimInteraction

      public static boolean claimInteraction(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer sp, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos markPos, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos... consulted)
      Gates a stack access and claims the click for it: every position in consulted must clear both vanilla's own protection and the right-click event, and only then is markPos marked against the vanilla click that follows.

      The cheap consults run across all positions before the first event fires, so a gesture refused for reaching outside the world border does not first announce itself to the listeners of a position it was never allowed to touch.

    • claimItemUse

      public static boolean claimItemUse(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer sp, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos markPos, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos... consulted)
      Gates a gesture that spends the held item and claims the click for it, the way claimInteraction(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos...) gates one that only reaches the block.

      A deposit is not the container access it resembles. Opening a chest costs nothing and its contents are gated again by whatever guards the screen; a deposit takes the stack straight out of the hand off the click, with nothing in between. It therefore requires permission to use an item here as well as permission to reach the block, matching the checks vanilla applies to item-driven interaction and claimPlacement(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos) applies to placement.

    • claimPlacement

      public static boolean claimPlacement(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer sp, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos againstPos, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos intoPos)
      Gates an item-driven placement of a block into intoPos against againstPos and claims the click for it. Vanilla checks both positions: the block being used governs the interaction, while the position being filled governs placement. They can fall on opposite sides of a protection boundary. The click landed on againstPos, so that is what is marked.

    • mayInteract

      public static boolean mayInteract(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer sp, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos pos)
      Fires PlayerInteractEvent.RightClickBlock for a stack access at pos so claim/protection mods can veto it, exactly as they would for a right-click on a vanilla container. true means the interaction is allowed.

      The event describes the interaction that is really happening: the face and point the player's own view ray meets. A mod that only asks who and where is unaffected, but one that logs what was clicked is told the truth rather than a placeholder.

    • mayUseItemOn

      public static boolean mayUseItemOn(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer sp, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos pos)
      Fires PlayerInteractEvent.RightClickBlock for an item-driven interaction at pos: a placement, or a deposit that spends the held stack. Either requires both access to the block and permission to use the held item on it, and a listener that refuses only the item refuses both.
